# dayjobdoor/dotfiles

> Ubuntu 26.04 (amd64, arm64) dotfiles managed entirely by mise: packages, system files, firewall, dotfiles, login shell and tools come from `mise bootstrap`. Modules (agent, server, full, secrets) are mise config environments on a base that includes the desktop; `djd` is the CLI. Ships agent sandbox and XFCE/RDP desktop images.

A coding agent runs `install.sh`, `djd`, `mise bootstrap`, `mise dot` or `mise trust` only on a machine that can be thrown away (a container or a VM), as AGENTS.md says. A person installs on a real machine as README.md describes. Never commit secrets; values go in age ciphertext through `djd secret set`. Start with AGENTS.md if you change the repository, and with README.md if you install it.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): install and the `djd doctor` check, modules, djd, secrets, desktop over RDP, VMs, remove, fork, development tasks, and a table of which doc to read when
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): why the design is what it is, covering symlinks, the install flow, modules, hooks, secrets, shell startup, the RDP service, Docker images, and CI decisions
- [Reference](docs/reference.md): layout tree, module contents, djd commands, make targets, bootstrap order and hooks, shell startup files, environment variables, XDG locations, RDP security and known limits, Docker images
- [Maintenance](docs/maintenance.md): workflows (including docs.yaml), the CI and release chain, timeouts, the release and publish rules, the workflow audit, repo tasks and the lock
- [Testing](docs/testing.md): what each CI job and test proves, the image, desktop and VM tests, the test map and where a new test goes, failure output, running CI with act
- [Guidance](docs/guidance.md): run CI locally, keep a VM after a failed test, test with multipass and OrbStack, update pinned tools, raise the mise release, set your git identity, move an npm config, keep an edit a program made, publish the first release, retry a failed publish, harden the repository settings
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules for coding agents, verification commands including the fast offline tests, where each kind of change and each new test goes, definition of done
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md): what must never be committed, vulnerability reporting, local override files, age secrets and their limits, GitHub tokens, workflows and releases with recommended repository settings, Docker, server and desktop hardening, known limits of the RDP service, checks
- [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md): colors, fonts and theme tokens (google-labs-code/design.md format)

## Configuration

The layout of the repository, with the purpose of each entry, is in [Reference](docs/reference.md#layout). These links are an index only.

- [mise-config/](mise-config/): the global mise config, linked as ~/.config/mise
- [home/](home/): dotfiles symlinked into ~
- [.mise/tasks/](.mise/tasks/): repo tasks
- [.mise/config.toml](.mise/config.toml): the short repo tasks and mise settings
- [install.sh](install.sh): the installer that `curl | sh` runs
- [Makefile](Makefile): `make <task>` runs `mise run <task>`
- [.mise/mise.lock](.mise/mise.lock): the pinned versions of the repo tools
- [.githooks/](.githooks/): the pre-commit hook
- [.agents/](.agents/): coding-agent skills for working on this repository
- [skills-lock.json](skills-lock.json): the source and hash of each skill in `.agents/`
- [.actrc](.actrc): the act runner images
- [.devcontainer/](.devcontainer/): the Docker images and compose.yaml
- [cloud-init/vm.yaml](cloud-init/vm.yaml): the cloud-init file for the VMs
- [tests/](tests/): the offline tests, VM and app checks, and the tree helper

## Optional

- [.github/workflows/](.github/workflows/): CI, docs, tag, release image and weekly full-module workflows
- [.github/dependabot.yml](.github/dependabot.yml): Dependabot for the pinned actions
